data.why: The page fetches the live public USGS GeoJSON earthquake feeds directly in the browser; there is no local dataset to prepare, and the repo's own test suite uses synthetic data generated inline in tests/, not fixture files.

goals: Select a region (all events, global M4.5+, California, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico) and read off the fitted Gutenberg-Richter b-value and its bootstrap uncertainty
Check the magnitude of completeness (Mc) for the region to judge how far down the catalog can be trusted
Look for an aftershock sequence and inspect the fitted Omori-Utsu decay (p, c) and its profile-likelihood range
Scan the hourly count chart for statistically flagged busy hours that may indicate a swarm or aftershock cluster
Watch the revision log to see how the catalog corrects itself (magnitude changes, id merges, deletions) while the page stays open
Compare depth-vs-magnitude patterns, e.g. spotting fixed default-depth solutions from automatic networks

review.summary: The tree matches the README's two jobs well (classic seismicity statistics and catalog-quality tracking) with sensible phases and accurate, well-sourced specific labels; 10 of 12 screens checked match their nodes. It needs a few fixes before filing: the revision-log feature is buried in an oversized f7, the newest-events list has no feature, two citations show the wrong thing (028 for Resume, 016 for the USGS click), and a couple of UI-noise actions should come out.
